result.rationale: In refreshOAuthTokens, when credential sync is enabled, the function returns a fetch Response object (`return response;` of `fetch(...)`). In googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts the diff changes to `const res = await refreshOAuthTokens(...); const token = res?.data;` — a fetch Response has no `.data` property, so `token` is undefined and `token.access_token` throws, silently swallowed by the surrounding try/catch, so the refresh fails whenever sync is enabled.

adjudication.rationale: In `GoogleCalendarService` the refresh path now uses `refreshOAuthTokens(...)` and then does `const token = res?.data; googleCredentials.access_token = token.access_token;` (apps-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts). But when credential sync is enabled, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns the result of `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, ...)`, i.e. a standard Fetch `Response` object (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts), which does not have a `.data` property. That makes `token` undefined and `token.access_token` will throw, causing refresh to fail.
